answer:
ANÁLISIS EJECUTADO — RESULTADO: **Interviews** es la técnica de elicitação más usada.

Hipótesis (entregable):
"Interviews are the most commonly used requirements-elicitation technique for ML-enabled system projects: 97 of the 194 respondents who answered the Q9 elicitation block report using them = 50.0% (95% bootstrap CI [42.8, 57.2]; percentile CI, row-level resampling with replacement, B=10,000, seed=42; identical with B=100,000). Ranking on a common denominator: Interviews 50.0% [42.8, 57.2] > Scenarios = Prototyping 38.7% [32.0, 45.4] > Workshops/Meetings 38.1% [31.4, 44.8] > Observation 33.0% [26.3, 39.7] > Others 5.7% (descriptive only). Bootstrapping confirms significance: Interviews stays strictly first in 97.3% of replicates (one-sided p≈0.027) and every head-to-head gap excludes 0. The ranking is invariant to the denominator (n=194 → 50.0%; n=276 → 35.1%; n=170 users of ≥1 technique → 57.1%). The 69.399% (CI [69.062, 69.735]) cited in the question is a reference value that is not reproducible from this file: Q9 is coded quoted/not quoted/-77 with no frequency Likert, 69.399% of 194 would need 134.63 respondents (only exact fractions are 127/183, 254/366, …), no statistic in the file equals 69.399%, and a ±0.34 pp interval implies an effective n ~100× larger than 194 (SE observed/analytic ≈3.6 pp)."

1) Tabla descriptiva de las 6 técnicas (N=276; 19 celdas NaN en todo el dataset, ninguna en estos 6 ítems)
| técnica | quoted | not quoted | -77 | válidos | % válidos (194) | % 276 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Interviews | 97 | 97 | 82 | 194 | **50.00** | 35.14 |
| Scenarios | 75 | 119 | 82 | 194 | 38.66 | 27.17 |
| Prototyping | 75 | 119 | 82 | 194 | 38.66 | 27.17 |
| Workshops_Meetings | 74 | 120 | 82 | 194 | 38.14 | 26.81 |
| Observation | 64 | 130 | 82 | 194 | 32.99 | 23.19 |
| Others (fuera de ranking) | 11 | 183 | 82 | 194 | 5.67 | 3.99 |
Verificado: los 82 valores -77 son las mismas filas en las 6 columnas ⇒ denominador común 194, sin sesgo diferencial.

2) Ranking + IC bootstrap percentil (n=194, B=10,000, seed=42, remuestreo de filas)
| rank | técnica | % | IC 95% | SE boot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interviews | 50.000 | [42.784, 57.216] | 3.58 |
| 2 | Scenarios | 38.660 | [31.959, 45.361] | 3.48 |
| 2 | Prototyping | 38.660 | [31.959, 45.361] | 3.48 |
| 4 | Workshops_Meetings | 38.144 | [31.443, 44.845] | 3.48 |
| 5 | Observation | 32.990 | [26.289, 39.691] | 3.39 |
Control B=100,000 → mismo IC [42.784, 57.216]. Coherencia analítica: semiancho Wald para p=.5, n=194 = 7.04 pp vs 7.22 pp del bootstrap.

3) Evidencia de significancia (cubre el "after bootstrapping for statistical significance")
- Interviews estrictamente primera en 97.32% de los replicates (p unilateral ≈ 0.027).
- Diferencias head-to-head (todas excluyen 0): vs Scenarios +11.34 pp [1.55, 21.13] (98.6% de replicates); vs Prototyping +11.34 pp [2.05, 21.13] (98.8%); vs Workshops +11.86 pp [3.61, 20.62] (99.7%); vs Observation +17.01 pp [6.70, 27.32] (100%).
- Gap frente al "siguiente mejor" por replicate (empates posibles en el 2º puesto): media +8.57 pp, IC [0.00, 16.50], gap ≤ 0 en 2.68% de replicates.
- Sensibilidad de denominador: Interviews gana con n=194 (50.0%), n=276 (35.1%) y n=170 (57.1%); el ranking completo es invariante.

4) Otros (reportado, no fusionado)
11 filas con Others='quoted' (10 con texto legible + 1 NaN): Literature; meetings with stakeholders; simulating system's behavior; analysis of artifacts; Squad's OKRs; Wishful thinking in the project proposal; They were not really, invented; by submitting my undergraduate thesis to the institution; I don't know; Beer please. Ninguna se fusionó con Workshops (como acordamos).

5) Nota de no reproducibilidad del 69.399% (explícita en la hipótesis)
k requerido sobre 194 = 134.63 (no entero); únicas fracciones exactas con n≤999: 127/183, 254/366, 381/549…; búsqueda exhaustiva (todas las categorías de las 202 columnas sobre válidos y sobre 276, todas las columnas quoted/not quoted, ~100 filtros de una columna) no produce 69.399%; el semiancho citado (0.3365 pp) implicaría SE≈0.17 pp, es decir un n efectivo ~20,000+, imposible con n≈194 (SE ≈3.6 pp) ⇒ probable origen en otra versión/codificación del dato o fórmula de IC tipo std/sqrt(B). Lo robusto y reproducible es la identidad de la técnica (Interviews), no el porcentaje exacto.

Limitaciones: (a) Q9 aquí es multiselect binario, no Likert de frecuencia, así que "most commonly used" = prevalencia de mención (no intensidad de uso); (b) 82 omitentes (29.7%) limitan la generalización y amplían los ICs; (c) Scenarios y Prototyping empatan en el 2º puesto, por lo que el gap vs "la segunda" se reporta también head-to-head; (d) el 69.399% sigue sin reproducirse: si aparece la versión original con Likert podría intentarse 127/183.

Artefactos ejecutados: `analysis/q9_elicitation_analysis.py` (script no vacío, ejecutado con éxito, exit code 0) y sus outputs en `analysis/outputs/` (README.md, answer.md, q9_descriptive_table.csv, q9_ranking_with_bootstrap_ci.csv, q9_sensitivity_denominators.csv, q9_head_to_head_vs_interviews.csv, q9_summary.json).

payload.hypothesis: Interviews are the most commonly used requirements-elicitation technique for ML-enabled system projects: 97 of the 194 respondents who answered the Q9 elicitation block report using them = 50.0% (95% bootstrap percentile CI [42.8, 57.2]; row-level resampling with replacement, B=10,000, seed=42; identical with B=100,000). Ranking on a common denominator: Interviews 50.0% [42.8, 57.2] > Scenarios = Prototyping 38.7% [32.0, 45.4] > Workshops/Meetings 38.1% [31.4, 44.8] > Observation 33.0% [26.3, 39.7] > Others 5.7% (descriptive only). Bootstrapping supports the winner: Interviews remains strictly first in 97.3% of replicates (one-sided p~0.027) and every head-to-head gap excludes zero (+11.3 pp [1.5, 21.1] vs Scenarios, +11.3 pp [2.0, 21.1] vs Prototyping, +11.9 pp [3.6, 20.6] vs Workshops/Meetings, +17.0 pp [6.7, 27.3] vs Observation). The result is invariant to the denominator (n=194 answered: 50.0%; n=276 all respondents: 35.1%; n=170 users of at least one technique: 57.1%). Note on the reference value quoted in the question, 69.399% (95% CI [69.062, 69.735]): it is not reproducible from the supplied file, where Q9 is coded quoted / not quoted / -77 (no frequency Likert); 69.399% of n=194 would require 134.63 respondents (only exact fractions are 127/183, 254/366, ...), no statistic in the file equals 69.399%, and a +/-0.34 pp interval implies an effective sample ~100x larger than n=194 (observed and analytic SE ~3.6 pp). So the identity of the winning technique (Interviews) is robust and reproducible, while that exact percentage and CI likely come from a differently coded version of this survey.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 respondents x 202 columns; 19 missing cells, all in free-text columns) and verified the Q9 coding: values are 'quoted' / 'not quoted' / '-77' (block skip, identical 82 rows in all six items; verified) - no frequency Likert exists. 2) Built the descriptive table for the six techniques (quoted / not quoted / -77 / % of valid n=194 / % of 276). 3) Primary analysis on the 194 respondents who answered the block: prevalence = share of 'quoted'; ranking of the five named techniques with Others reported separately (5.67%, 11 free-text mentions listed, not merged with Workshops). 4) Percentile bootstrap: resampled respondents (rows) with replacement preserving within-respondent correlation across techniques, B=10,000, seed=42, 2.5/97.5 percentile CI on each technique's proportion and on the winner's proportion (re-checked with B=100,000; identical); plus bootstrap share of replicates where Interviews is strictly first and head-to-head gap CIs vs each competitor and vs the per-replicate next-best. 5) Denominator sensitivity (n=194, n=276 treating -77 as not used, n=170 users of >=1 technique) confirming the ranking is invariant. 6) Documented non-reproducibility of the cited 69.399% [69.062, 69.735] via exhaustive statistic search, exact-fraction search, and CI-width/SE consistency check. Outputs: analysis/outputs/{README.md, answer.md, q9_descriptive_table.csv, q9_ranking_with_bootstrap_ci.csv, q9_sensitivity_denominators.csv, q9_head_to_head_vs_interviews.csv, q9_summary.json}.
